scenes.say: Every web app is haunted. This is Ghost Crew: a skeleton for browser QA, built with Kiro for Kiroween.

Before every release, someone walks the pages by hand. Tab with the keyboard. Type a strange name into the form. Check it on a phone. Things slip through. This little inn has fifteen bugs, planted on purpose.
With Ghost Crew, you write a ghost instead. A few lines of YAML: which page to haunt, what to click, and which senses to use.
Then you summon the crew. One real Chrome, a private context for every ghost, four walking at once. Poltergeist, the accessibility app, comes back with nine hauntings in a few seconds.

Every ghost brings back a spirit photograph. The page turns to silver, and every problem glows, numbered to match the list. A missing alt text. A close button with no name. A Book now button the keyboard can never reach. Flip the switch to see the living page.

The second app, Phantom Form, types what real people type. An emoji in a name turns into broken characters. Markup in the name field runs as code. A long name crashes the page. Most curses got through.
Fix the bugs, pass last night's report as the baseline, and the record shows what you exorcised. Every haunting is gone, and nothing new appeared. The house is quiet.
Both apps sit on the same skeleton. Each app is about two hundred lines: a few senses, a theme, and its own crew. A new kind of ghost is a single file.

It was built in Kiro Crew, spec first. Steering fixes the vocabulary and the exact shape of a ghost. Hooks check every ghost on save, and run the tests before the agent stops. An MCP server gives any Kiro agent five tools to write and summon ghosts. And a Kiro Crew app adds a Ghost Captain, with an optional midnight patrol.
Every night at midnight, GitHub Actions haunts the inn again and publishes the records. Point it at your own site with one n p x command.
Ghost Crew. Let the ghosts find it, before your users do.
